item: Federal tax character of Kalshi event contracts
detail: No IRS ruling, revenue procedure, or notice classifies Kalshi event contracts as section 1256 contracts. Practitioners disagree: some take 60/40 treatment on Form 6781, others report capital-asset or ordinary treatment; Kalshi's own tax documentation is limited to 1099-INT, 1099-MISC, 1099-B (crypto transfers), 1099-DA, and a P&L statement, and Kalshi states its information is not tax advice. The Bipartisan Policy Center (Aug 2026) documents the unresolved uncertainty. Impact on healthcare eligibility: none - under any characterization the gains are unearned investment income included in MAGI. Consult a tax professional.
notes: Value intentionally left blank: no official source confirms a single tax character. If section 1256 applies, see IRS Form 6781 (60/40, mark-to-market).

item: Do hours spent trading on Kalshi count as qualifying work?
detail: Federal 'work' (42 CFR 435.552(b)) covers paid, in-kind, and unpaid work other than community service; the CMS preamble and DHCS ACWDL 25-30 include self-employment/business owners/independent contractors. No official source addresses hours spent personally trading event contracts/futures on one's own account. IRS Topic 429 treats own-account trading gains as not self-employment earnings - relevant context, but Medicaid 'work' is not defined by SE-tax status, so the county's determination controls. Confirm with the county Medi-Cal office in writing before relying on trading hours.
notes: Verified alternatives that need no earned income: $580 MAGI-based income in a qualifying month, 80 hours structured community service, work program, or at least half-time school.

item: Effective-date framing differs across official sources
value: Three official framings
detail: CMS: states must implement no later than January 1, 2027 (or earlier at state option). CRS Report R48755: effective beginning December 31, 2026, or sooner at state option. DHCS member outreach letter (Aug 2026): the rules will not go into effect until March 2027 (existing members are assessed at six-month renewals, which begin March 1, 2027 in California). These are consistent in practice - coverage months governed by the requirement begin with January 2027, and existing members are first assessed at renewal - but the differing phrasing is flagged for review.
notes: Compare CRS R48755 (congress.gov) and DHCS MEDIL I26-25 (dhcs.ca.gov).

item: Caretaker exemption age wording (official sources conflict, including CMS with itself)
value: Exemption is for caregivers of a child 13 or younger
detail: CMS fact sheet, 'Who is Affected?' paragraph: exempt individuals include 'parents and caretakers of children under 14 years of age or people with disabilities.' The same fact sheet's Exemptions chart says 'a dependent child 13 years of age and under.' DHCS ACWDL 25-30 and AB 2161 / WIC 14005.69(b)(2)(E) say 'a dependent child 13 years of age and under'; the DHCS member page says 'children ages 0-13'; DHCS MEDIL I26-25 says parents or caregivers of dependent children aged 14 and above must engage. The DHCS Tracking page phrases it as adults without children under 13, which read literally would wrongly exclude parents of 13-year-olds. Louisiana's official Medicaid page says 'a child under age 14.' Flagged: the CMS fact sheet contradicts itself, and one DHCS page contradicts the rest. Operative California guidance (ACWDL 25-30, AB 2161) is 13 years of age and under.
notes: Verified 2026-10-18 against the CMS fact sheet, DHCS ACWDL 25-30, the DHCS member page, AB 2161, and Louisiana LDH. See also DHCS Tracking Federal Impact page (dhcs.ca.gov/tracking-federal-impact-medi-cal-eligibility/).

item: $580 income-standard wording differs across DHCS materials
value: Income from any source vs. work at a job and earn
detail: Hierarchy now available: (1) 42 CFR 435.552(f) + CA Welf. & Inst. Code 14005.69(e)(6) measure the $580 test as MAGI-based monthly income (earned + unearned); (2) DHCS MEDIL outreach letter tells members 'income from any source of at least $580 (before taxes)'; (3) DHCS preliminary ACWDL 25-30 said 'total gross income' including dividends etc.; (4) the DHCS member-facing Medi-Cal Changes webpage still says 'work at a job and earn at least $580 a month'; CMS fact-sheet prose also says 'earning' while its table says 'have monthly income.' The regulation/statute control over simplified webpage prose, but the inconsistent member-facing wording remains flagged because members will read the webpage first.
notes: Compare DHCS Medi-Cal Changes page (dhcs.ca.gov/medi-cal/updates/medi-cal-changes/) with eCFR 435.552(f). If a county worker applies a wages-only reading, cite 435.552(f)(2) and WIC 14005.69(e)(6) and request review/appeal rights.

item: RESOLVED: $580 test is MAGI-based (net rental/gains, unearned counts); REMAINING: monthly trading measurement + household allocation
value: MAGI-based monthly income for the individual's MAGI household (42 CFR 435.552(f)(2)); monthly trading doc method and household allocation = blank/unverified
detail: Update 2026-10-18 (session da6d01ac): 42 CFR 435.552(f)(2) (effective July 31, 2026) requires monthly income to be determined from MAGI-based income for the MAGI-based household under 42 CFR 435.603; CA Welf. & Inst. Code 14005.69(e)(6) (AB 2161, Sept 14, 2026) adopts MAGI-based methods for the individual MAGI household budget. Gross-vs-net is therefore resolved: use MAGI concepts (net rental Schedule E profit, interest incl. tax-exempt add-back, net capital/trading gains with loss limits) - not gross rents or gross trade proceeds. Still unverified: (a) the county's month-by-month documentation for realized Kalshi gains/losses (incl. loss months and lump-sum-month-only counting under 435.603(e)(1)); (b) allocation of household MAGI to the individual when the MAGI household has multiple members. ACWDL's individual-assessment rule (another person's compliance cannot satisfy yours) still applies.
notes: Supersedes both the original 'not confirmed' note and the preliminary ACWDL 'total gross income' update. Keep monthly P&L, rent ledger (gross + expenses), and bank interest records.

That figure matches neither the 2025 ($15,650) nor the 2026 ($15,960) 100% FPL guideline for one person. Flagged as a possible typo or reference to a different standard in DHCS member materials.

item: Six-month averaging: seasonal workers only (federal) vs fluctuating income (DHCS wording)
value: Federal averaging limited to seasonal workers; broader DHCS fluctuating-income wording unconfirmed for traders
detail: 42 CFR 435.552(g) and Welf. & Inst. Code 14005.69(e)(7) grant 6-month averaging to a seasonal worker as described in IRC 45R(d)(5)(B). DHCS ACWDL 25-30 (preliminary) and the MEDIL member letter describe averaging for people whose hours change frequently / whose gross income fluctuates (listing unemployment, SDI, retirement, dividends, etc.). A full-time trader's variable monthly gains are not obviously 'seasonal work.' Do not plan around averaging Kalshi gains over 6 months unless the county confirms eligibility for averaging; the safer verified route is a single qualifying month at or above $580 MAGI-based income (CA-13).
notes: Compare DHCS ACWDL 25-30 and MEDIL I26-25 averaging language. Flagged for county clarification.

item: Do hours managing your own rental property count as qualifying work?
detail: No official source reviewed answers this. Established pieces: Medicaid work includes self-employment (CMS preamble; ACWDL 25-30); fees for managing others' property are business/SE income (IRS Topic 414); rent from your own property is generally not SE earnings (IRS Schedule E instructions) and rental activity is generally passive for tax-loss purposes (IRS Pub. 527). None of those tax rules defines Medicaid 'work,' and DHCS has not published whether documented self-management hours (leasing, repairs coordination, bookkeeping for your own units) count toward 80 hours, or what proof would be required. Ask the county before relying on these hours; the $580 MAGI-based income month and structured community service remain verified alternatives.
notes: Value intentionally left blank: no official source confirms it. If you are paid management fees by third parties, that activity is earned business income - a different fact pattern (IN-04).

item: $580 income standard: three different official phrasings
value: 'total gross income' (ACWDL 25-30) vs 'income from any source of at least $580 (before taxes)' (member letter) vs 'work at a job and earn at least $580 a month' (member page)
detail: DHCS ACWDL 25-30 (county instruction, labelled preliminary): 'An individual's total gross income for a month must meet or exceed this amount.' DHCS MEDIL I26-25 member outreach letter: 'Have an income from any source of at least $580 (before taxes) in any month since your last renewal.' DHCS Medi-Cal Changes member page: 'Work at a job and earn at least $580 a month.' California statute WIC 14005.69(e)(6): total monthly income 'using modified adjusted gross income (MAGI)-based financial methods... for their individual MAGI-based household budget.' CMS: 'monthly income that is not less than the federal minimum wage multiplied by 80 hours.' The member page's 'work at a job' phrasing is the narrowest and conflicts with the operative county instruction and the statute.
notes: Practical effect: gross rent, interest, and trading gains can be argued to count under the ACWDL and statute, but the narrowest public phrasing says 'work at a job'. Confirm with the county before relying on non-wage income.

item: School enrollment standard: 'at least half-time' vs 'part-time'
value: At least half-time (CMS, DHCS member page, AB 2161) vs part-time or full-time (ACWDL 25-30) vs at least part time (member letter)
detail: CMS fact sheet: 'Enroll in an educational program at least half time.' DHCS Medi-Cal Changes page: 'Go to school at least half-time (usually two or three classes, or about six to eight credits each semester).' California statute WIC 14005.69(e)(4): 'enrolled in an educational program at least half-time.' DHCS ACWDL 25-30 qualifying-activities table: 'Go to school part-time or full-time.' DHCS MEDIL I26-25 member letter: 'Go to school at least part time in any month since your last renewal,' adding that students below part time may combine class and school-activity hours with work, community service, or job training to reach 80 hours. ACWDL 25-30's worked example also refers to enrollment 'at least half-time.'
notes: The statute and CMS both say at least half-time; two DHCS documents say part-time. Flagged rather than reconciled.

item: Six-month renewal start date framing
value: January 1, 2027 (law, ACWDL 25-31, DHCS Implementation Plan) vs March 1, 2027 (DHCS member pages)
detail: Section 71107 of P.L. 119-21 is effective January 1, 2027; DHCS ACWDL 25-31 states 'Effective January 1, 2027, states must conduct Medi-Cal eligibility renewals every six months for adult Medi-Cal members enrolled in the MAGI New Adult Group,' and the DHCS Implementation Plan lists 'Six-Month Renewals (Effective January 1, 2027).' The DHCS Medi-Cal Changes page and the Tracking page both say six-month eligibility checks start March 1, 2027. The DHCS member outreach letter says the 6-Month Renewal Rule begins January 2027 but that both rules 'will not go into effect until March 2027.' ACWDL 25-30 explains the mechanism: existing members transition to the six-month cycle at their next 2027 renewal.
notes: Reconciled in practice (statutory date January 1, 2027; first member-facing checks March 1, 2027), but the public pages state different dates. Flagged for review.

item: Whose income counts - individual-only vs household
value: Individual's own income (California guidance) vs 'can be deemed from other household members' (secondary sources)
detail: DHCS ACWDL 25-30 states Medi-Cal eligibility is determined at the individual level, that 'All individuals must independently meet the participation criteria; one individual's compliance cannot be used to satisfy another's requirement,' and that the income test is 'An individual's total gross income for a month.' California statute WIC 14005.69(e)(6) refers to income 'for their individual MAGI-based household budget.' Secondary analyses (Justice in Aging, law-firm summaries of CMS-2454-IFC) report that CMS uses the individual's MAGI-based income and that the amount can be earned or unearned and 'can be deemed from other household members.' No official California source supports the household-deeming statement, and ACWDL 25-30's two-adult example directly rejects using a partner's hours.
notes: Carried forward from the earlier FL-06 (resolved in part). The individual-level reading is the one supported by California's operative county guidance.

item: Whether rental income, savings interest, and Kalshi trading gains count toward the $580 test
value: Counts: the $580 route is measured by MAGI-based income, which includes unearned rental, interest, and capital gains; no official source names these three streams individually
detail: 42 CFR 435.552(e)(6) and (f) measure the $580 route by MAGI-based income for the individual's MAGI household; 42 CFR 435.603 ties MAGI-based income to 26 U.S.C. 36B(d)(2)(B) (AGI plus tax-exempt interest and specified add-backs). AGI includes net rental income, interest, and net capital gains. California's statute uses MAGI-based methods (WIC 14005.69(e)(6), as amended by AB 2161), and the earlier SB 164 text expressly listed “unemployment benefits, state disability insurance, retirement income, or dividends” as included income — all unearned. DHCS's member letter says “income from any source.” Residual open issue: how a county documents month-by-month trading P&L (FL-06). Kalshi tax character remains FL-01.
notes: Resolved 2026-10-18 (session arena/5711b968) by applying the operative definition; the three streams are not named individually in any official list. This is a statement of the rule, not a county determination and not a documentation standard.

item: P.L. 119-21 is published under two different names
value: One Big Beautiful Bill Act and Working Families Tax Cuts Act (WFTCA / WFTCL)
detail: CMS guidance states 'Public Law (P.L.) 119-21, known as the Working Families Tax Cut Act (WFTCA), which was signed into law on July 4, 2025.' The 2027 federal payment-parameters rule cites 'Section 71305 of the WFTC legislation.' The IRS attributes the removal of APTC repayment caps to 'the Working Families Tax Cuts Act,' while CRS attributes the PTC provisions to 'the FY2025 budget reconciliation law (P.L. 119-21)' and the Medicaid community engagement requirement to section 71119 of the same law. All refer to the July 4, 2025 statute.
notes: Not a substantive conflict; flagged so a reader comparing citations is not misled.

item: Absence-based statement about the premium tax credit
value: 'No work requirement on marketplace coverage'
detail: HealthCare.gov's premium tax credit glossary lists eligibility as turning on household information, estimated income, and income between 100% and 400% FPL, and contains no work, hours, or community-engagement condition. The statement 'the ACA premium tax credit rules contain no work-hours or community engagement test' is therefore an absence-based statement: it is supported by the cited official page's silence, not by an affirmative official statement that no such test exists.
notes: Marked as an absence-based claim rather than an affirmative official finding.
